correctness.rationale: For fixed sets of label-2 vertices, every other label is forced to its minimum feasible value by positivity. Any optimum uses at most two label-2 vertices per shore. Three support types are then strictly or weakly dominated, leaving exactly six cases whose costs are C20,C02,C11,C21,C12,C22. The case split covers all quantifiers n>=3 and all positive real weights. Exhaustive finite checks independently agree with the formula but are not used as proof.

value.rationale: Weighted Roman domination was introduced specifically to model heterogeneous vertex costs, and the initiating paper emphasizes that weights change the optimal strategy even on complete bipartite graphs. Crowns are the canonical one-factor deletion of balanced bicliques; the theorem gives a complete exact optimization for arbitrary positive costs and shows precisely how one missing matched neighbor creates six competing support regimes. This is structurally informative rather than a routine unweighted substitution.
